week_in_brief: The market is moving again — but your lead sources aren't where they used to be.

items.headline: Buyer Demand Just Hit Its Highest Level in Two Years
items.whats_happening: April and May 2026 data shows buyer demand jumping 6% while inventory climbs 2–4% week over week — the best combination of activity and supply balance since May 2024. Spring momentum is real. Buyers are negotiating again, contracts are moving, and agents with strong market knowledge are winning deals in a less competitive environment.
items.so_what: After a year of "wait and see," buyers are back. Your marketing should shift from urgency-based offers to value-based positioning — agent expertise in a shifting buyer's market, fair negotiation outcomes, and local market intelligence that helps clients win without overpaying.

items.headline: Meta Just Overtook Google in Global Ad Revenue
items.whats_happening: Meta is projected to generate $243.46 billion in global ad revenue in 2026, surpassing Google's $239.54 billion for the first time in history. Meta's growth rate hit 24.1% year-over-year, driven by Reels momentum, Advantage+ AI automation, and WhatsApp expansion. Meanwhile, Google's search environment is getting noisier — AI Overviews are consuming top-of-page real estate and top-ranking pages saw click-through rates drop 18–34% once AI answers appeared above the fold.
items.so_what: If your paid strategy is still Google-first, you're betting on yesterday's leader. Test Meta's Advantage+ automation now — Reels and feed placements are delivering measurable ROI for local service businesses, and the targeting is getting sharper as the platform scales. Google isn't dead, but it's no longer the default winner.

items.headline: AI Search Is Rewiring Agent Discovery — and Rankings Don't Matter Anymore
items.whats_happening: Google's May 2026 Core Update severed the link between traditional page-one rankings and AI citation visibility. Research shows top-10 rankers accounted for 76% of AI citations in mid-2025, but only 38% by early 2026. Consumers now use conversational AI tools and natural-language search to ask questions about neighborhoods, property fit, and local market conditions — and they're bypassing agent-first discovery entirely. The algorithm now prioritizes passage structure and information consistency across independent sources over backlink profiles.
items.so_what: Ranking #1 on Google doesn't guarantee you show up in the AI answer. Your content needs to be structured for three simultaneous layers: rankings, citations, and agent-source-trust. That means agent bios with demonstrable local expertise, video walkthroughs showcasing neighborhood knowledge, verified reviews, and answers to buyer questions written in clear, structured language. If you're not optimizing for AI discoverability, you're invisible to the fastest-growing search behavior.

items.headline: MLSs Are Fracturing — and Your Zillow Feed Might Disappear Next
items.whats_happening: A federal judge in Chicago ordered MRED to restore Zillow's listing feed after Compass pressured the MLS to cut it off. Nashville's Realtracs is threatening a June 1 shutdown. Four other MLS signed exclusive data deals with Compass. The power struggle between portal access and MLS control is creating real volatility in buyer-side lead flow and listing visibility — and it's not getting resolved anytime soon.
items.so_what: Prtal syndication is no longer guaranteed infrastructure. Invest in owned organic search, direct buyer relationships, and agent-level SEO now. If your lead generation strategy assumes Zillow and Realtor.com will always carry your listings, you're one MLS board decision away from going dark.

this_weeks_take: Tem market is moving. Buyers are back. Inventory is rising. And the old playbook — Google SEO plus Zillow syndication — is cracking on both sides at the same time. The brokerages that win this cycle will be the ones who built their own discovery infrastructure before the platforms made the decision for them.
